fixes.explanation: Esau is a Bible name, baker, but he isn't in this passage. Paul says, "Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise." (Galatians 4:28). Isaac is the one he compares them to. Esau was Isaac's son (Genesis 25:26), so you're in the right family, just one name off.

Yes, baker. Paul says the son by the slave woman "…was born according to the flesh…" (Galatians 4:23). That son was Ishmael, Hagar's boy (Genesis 16:15). His brother Isaac was different, because God had told Abraham that Sarah would bear him a son (Genesis 17:19). So "flesh" marks the birth of the slave woman's son, and "promise" marks the birth of the free woman's son.

Right on, baker. The son by the free woman "…was born through the promise." (Galatians 4:23). That son was Isaac, and God had said ahead of time that Sarah would bear Abraham a son (Genesis 17:19). His birth was tied to what God had said. The other son, Ishmael, is the one Paul describes as born according to the flesh.

That's right, baker. The believers belong to the free woman, not the slave woman (Galatians 4:31). Paul had just called them children of promise like Isaac (Galatians 4:28), so this is where he was heading. And he says "we," so he counts himself in with them.
